brief.prompt: Create a two-minute Physical AI inference film centered on a fresh simulation experiment. Use more Nebius Token Factory and other model families. Remove NVIDIA branding and model usage, and do not reuse footage from the executive film.
brief.audience: C-suite and technical leaders evaluating Physical AI inference
brief.goal: Show how model-generated plans, physical simulation, measured outcomes, and visual evaluation form an inspectable development loop.
brief.tone: Cinematic, clear, technical claims grounded in the recorded experiment.

title: Intelligence,
tested.
scenes.subtitle: Inference meets the physical world.
scenes.narration: Physical A I turns decisions into motion. Simulation lets us test what those decisions actually do.

title: Start with
a goal.
scenes.subtitle: Orange cube. Cyan target. A plan to connect them.
scenes.narration: Start with a goal: move the orange cube into the cyan target.

title: Qwen proposes a route.
scenes.subtitle: A structured task becomes model-generated waypoints.
scenes.narration: Through Nebius Token Factory, Qwen proposes a straight route. Its returned waypoints become the controller’s input.

title: Run the plan in physics.
scenes.subtitle: A scripted controller executes the returned waypoints.
scenes.narration: The controller executes that plan in MuJoCo. In the clear scene, the cube reaches the target.

title: Same plan.
New obstacle.
scenes.subtitle: Replay the original waypoints with an obstacle in the path.
scenes.narration: Add an obstacle and replay the same plan. The task fails. A changed world needs a new decision.

title: Verify the
verdict.
scenes.subtitle: This visual assessment incorrectly reports success.
labels: ORIGINAL FINAL FRAME / CUBE OUTSIDE THE TARGET
scenes.narration: Vision models also need evaluation. In this case, Mini C P M reports success, but the simulation disagrees.
source_notes: An observed false positive; checked against recorded state.

title: Ground the next request.
scenes.subtitle: Images, measured state, and geometry inform the revision.
labels: ACTUAL SIMULATOR MEASUREMENT / DISTANCE TO GOAL CENTER
scenes.narration: MuJoCo measures the failed outcome. Send that state, the images, and obstacle geometry into the next inference.

title: MiniMax proposes a detour.
scenes.subtitle: The model returns a new route for the same controller.
scenes.narration: Using images and simulator evidence, MiniMax proposes a new route around the obstacle.

title: Test the
revised decision.
scenes.subtitle: Same task. Same obstacle. A new route.
scenes.narration: Execute the revised waypoints in the same simulation. The robot takes the detour and reaches the original target.

title: Measure
what changed.
scenes.subtitle: Distance from cube center to goal center, in this experiment.
scenes.narration: Compare outcomes using recorded state. The task, obstacle, and success criteria stay the same.

title: Evaluate the evidence.
scenes.subtitle: Separate model judgments, checked against simulation state.
scenes.narration: MiniMax evaluates both outcomes. Check those judgments against measured state, and preserve the evidence.

scenes.eyebrow: THREE MODEL FAMILIES / ONE DEVELOPMENT LOOP
title: Choose models for the job.
scenes.subtitle: Planning, visual feedback, revision, and evaluation.
labels: FIVE NEW INFERENCE CALLS THROUGH NEBIUS TOKEN FACTORY
scenes.narration: Connect models through Token Factory. Test decisions in simulation. Keep the evidence together.

title: Build an inference loop.
scenes.subtitle: Open the project. Change the task. Test the next decision.
scenes.narration: Build an inference loop with Nebius Token Factory. Plan. Simulate. Evaluate. Revise. Keep improving.
